provenance.quote:

contests.title: Clawson — Renshaw Senior Apartments sale

provenance.quote:
Clawson
                                           City of Clawson Property Disposition Proposal 26-1
Shall the City Council of the City of Clawson, Oakland County, Michigan, be granted the authority and approval from the City of
Clawson voters to sell or dispose of real property described as follows:

121 Renshaw Ave, Clawson, MI 48017, more particularly described as:

Tax Parcel I.D. #’s: 25-03-103-004, 25-03-103-005, 25-03-103-006, 25-03-103-013, 25-03-103-014, and 25-03-107-035;

and that the proceeds from such sale or disposition of the real property described above be approved for use on the sustainment
and improvement of senior services in the City of Clawson?

Explanatory Statement

The Renshaw Senior Apartments, located at 121 Renshaw Avenue, is a 15-unit residential building owned and operated by the City
of Clawson. Under the City Charter, City-owned property valued above the charter threshold cannot be sold without the approval of
a majority of electors voting on the question at a City election.

This proposal asks voters whether the City Council may sell or otherwise dispose of the Renshaw property. If approved, the proceeds
of any sale would be directed toward the sustainment and improvement of senior services in the City of Clawson. Approval would
authorize, but would not by itself complete, a sale; the City Council would still determine the terms, process, and timeline of any
disposition, including arrangements affecting current residents.

A “YES” vote grants the City Council the authority to sell or dispose of the Renshaw property, with proceeds dedicated to senior
services.

A “NO” vote denies that authority, and the City would retain ownership and continue to operate the property.

measures.questionText:
Clawson
                                           City of Clawson Property Disposition Proposal 26-1
Shall the City Council of the City of Clawson, Oakland County, Michigan, be granted the authority and approval from the City of
Clawson voters to sell or dispose of real property described as follows:

121 Renshaw Ave, Clawson, MI 48017, more particularly described as:

Tax Parcel I.D. #’s: 25-03-103-004, 25-03-103-005, 25-03-103-006, 25-03-103-013, 25-03-103-014, and 25-03-107-035;

and that the proceeds from such sale or disposition of the real property described above be approved for use on the sustainment
and improvement of senior services in the City of Clawson?

Explanatory Statement

The Renshaw Senior Apartments, located at 121 Renshaw Avenue, is a 15-unit residential building owned and operated by the City
of Clawson. Under the City Charter, City-owned property valued above the charter threshold cannot be sold without the approval of
a majority of electors voting on the question at a City election.

This proposal asks voters whether the City Council may sell or otherwise dispose of the Renshaw property. If approved, the proceeds
of any sale would be directed toward the sustainment and improvement of senior services in the City of Clawson. Approval would
authorize, but would not by itself complete, a sale; the City Council would still determine the terms, process, and timeline of any
disposition, including arrangements affecting current residents.

A “YES” vote grants the City Council the authority to sell or dispose of the Renshaw property, with proceeds dedicated to senior
services.

A “NO” vote denies that authority, and the City would retain ownership and continue to operate the property.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews 0.0927 mill and restores 0.0073 mill for a total 0.10 mill on taxable real and personal property for 2028–2037 for Detroit Zoo services. Funds pass through the Zoological Authority and receive annual independent audits. Estimated first-year collections are $8,831,012.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve renewal and restoration to 0.10 mill.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds 0.2 mill on all taxable property for 2026–2035 for public historical museum services, including the Charles H. Wright, Detroit Historical and Dossin Great Lakes museums. Estimated 2026 revenue is $17,733,800. After authority administration costs, 15% of Oakland County revenue returns to the county to support historical museums.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the ten-year historical museum millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews library-tax authority up to 0.52 mill a year for six years starting with the July 2027 levy, replacing authority expiring in 2026. It funds a contract giving city residents and local business employers and employees full Baldwin Public Library privileges on the same basis as Birmingham users. Estimated first-year revenue is $440,405.

Authorizes 7 mills in the City of the Village of Clarkston from July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2031 to continue police, firefighting, fire protection and emergency response services. Estimated first-year collections are $457,116.

Authorizes the council to sell or otherwise dispose of the city-owned 15-unit Renshaw Senior Apartments at 121 Renshaw Avenue, with proceeds dedicated to sustaining and improving senior services. Approval does not complete a sale; the council still sets terms, process, timing and arrangements affecting current residents.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize sale or disposition with proceeds dedicated to senior services.
measureRecords.noMeans: Deny that authority; the city retains ownership and continues to operate the property.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds 1 mill for 2027–2031 exclusively for the city’s library services contract, subject to legal reductions including Headlee rollbacks. Estimated first-year revenue at the full rate is $175,000.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the five-year library services millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Amends the charter to replace an expiring capital-improvements tax with 1 mill for ten years starting with the July 2027 levy. Funds may support parks, facilities, land, pathways and equipment such as fire trucks and heavy equipment, and cannot fund operations or payroll. Estimated first-year revenue is $5,412,997.
Authorizes the city to sell its vacant parcel at 4039 Pontiac Trail, parcel 18-15-428-017.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize sale of the specified vacant parcel.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $75 million in unlimited-tax bonds for roads, sidewalks, ramps, drainage, lighting, traffic controls and related facilities, including necessary water and sewer work. Each series may last up to 30 years. Estimated millage is 3.360 in 2027 and a 2.400 annual average.
Amends the charter to renew 0.70 mill a year for five years beginning in 2027 for parks, recreation, playgrounds and animal shelter purposes. Estimated first-year revenue is $2,925,250.
Renews 0.20 mill for 2027–2031 solely for services, activities and programs for older persons, replacing authority expiring with the 2026 levy. Estimated first-year revenue is $835,664.

Authorizes up to $50 million in unlimited-tax bonds for a fire station, a township police building, equipment and related site work. Each series may last up to 20 years. Estimated millage is 0.2350 in the first authorized year and a 0.4380 annual average.
Renews up to 3.9509 mills for police protection at the rolled-back rate, with printed levy years 2027 through 2035. Estimated first-year revenue is $3,228,587.

Authorizes up to $18.6 million in unlimited-tax bonds, payable over no more than ten years from issue, for paved nonmotorized pathways and related improvements in the township and Wolverine Lake village under their parks and recreation plans. Estimated millage is 0.5986 in the first year and a 0.5989 annual average.

Renews 1.85 mills and adds 0.47 mill for a total 2.32 mills for 2027–2032 for fire and emergency medical services. Estimated first-year revenue is $2,731,774. A small portion collected from Downtown Development Authority properties supports that authority.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve renewal and increase to 2.32 mills.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Replaces an expired police levy, which had rolled back to 2.8282 mills, with up to 3.2 mills from December 2026 through December 2029 for police, staff, operations, capital costs and school resource officers. Estimated first-year revenue is $7,781,495.86. Some revenue from designated development areas is captured by their authorities as required by law.

Adds up to 1.1 mills on all taxable township property for 2026–2035 for library operations, maintenance, supplies, equipment and other lawful library purposes. Revenue goes to the township public library; estimated first-year collections are $2,560,000.

Renews the current rolled-back rate of up to 0.6809 mill for ten years beginning with the December 2027 levy for park land, trails, facilities, programs and services, including acquisition, operations, maintenance and improvements. Estimated first-year revenue is $1,462,309.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the parks and recreation millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews the rolled-back rate of up to 0.1580 mill from December 2027 through December 2036 for safety paths, trails, boardwalks, land and rights-of-way. Estimated first-year revenue is $351,302, disbursed to the township.

Replaces expired fire and emergency medical authority at the 2026 rolled-back rate of up to 2.8846 mills from December 2026 through December 2029, including Lake Orion village. It supports emergency services, personnel, equipment and facilities. Estimated first-year revenue is $8,079,234.79; designated development authorities may capture revenue from their areas as required by law.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the replacement fire and emergency medical millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds up to 0.4000 mill from December 2026 through December 2029, including Lake Orion village, for more fire and emergency medical staff, wages and benefits, response capability, equipment and station improvements. Estimated first-year revenue is $1,119,907.94; designated development authorities may capture revenue from their areas as required by law.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the additional fire and emergency medical millage.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $13.3 million in unlimited-tax bonds, payable over no more than 20 years from issue, for library additions, renovations, equipment, children’s resources, community spaces, technology, accessibility and related sites. Estimated millage is 0.3116 in 2027 and a 0.3117 annual average.
Renews 0.8822 mill on taxable real and personal property for 2026–2035 to staff, maintain and operate the fire department for township residents. Estimated first-year revenue is $2,994,579.65.
Renews 1.3352 mills on taxable real and personal property for 2026–2035 for police staffing, maintenance and operations. Estimated first-year revenue is $4,532,219.12.

Amends the charter to dedicate 0.75 mill of the existing general property-tax levy to public street and road improvements, maintenance and construction from the July 2027 levy through the July 2030 levy. It reallocates existing taxes and does not change the authorized maximum rate.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Dedicate the stated share of existing taxes to roads.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Replaces the fixed $2,000 competitive-bidding threshold with purchasing and contracting limits set by council resolution. It allows a purchasing agent, awards based on the bid most advantageous to the village, and council-authorized work by village staff when permitted by ordinance.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the revised purchasing and contracting rules.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the charter rule requiring contracts over $2,000 to go to the lowest responsible bidder through competitive bidding.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $240 million in unlimited-tax bonds for school safety, heating and cooling, accessible playgrounds, buildings, early childhood facilities, technology, career equipment, additions, sites and buses. Each series may last up to 20 years. Estimated new-bond millage is 0.84 in the first year and a 1.30 annual average. Combined existing and proposed bond debt millage is expected at or below 3.80. Audited bond proceeds cannot fund salaries, repairs, maintenance or operating expenses.

Authorizes up to $171 million in unlimited-tax bonds for STEAM and maker programs, buildings and additions, athletic fields, playgrounds, technology, sites, health, safety, security and energy conservation. Each series may last up to 20 years. Estimated new-bond millage is 0.95 in the first year and a 1.32 annual average. Combined existing and proposed bond debt millage is expected at or below 3.20. Audited bond proceeds cannot fund salaries, repairs, maintenance or operating expenses.

Replaces, restores and extends operating-tax authority for 2027–2046, replacing authority scheduled to expire in 2035. Although 20 mills are authorized, no more than 18 may be levied; two mills are available for future constitutional rollbacks. Principal residences and other legally exempt property are excluded. Estimated 2027 revenue is $6,742,038.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the replacement and restoration within the 18 mill levy cap.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews 19.8592 mills of operating-tax authority for 2028–2032 while continuing a statutory levy of no more than 18 mills. Principal residences and other legally exempt property are excluded. The prior authorization expires with the 2027 levy; estimated revenue at an 18 mill levy in 2028 is $1,887,000.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the authority within the 18 mill levy limit.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $97.6 million in unlimited-tax bonds for school safety, buildings, early childhood and career spaces, music and athletic facilities, technology, sites and playgrounds. Each series may last up to 30 years. Estimated new-bond millage is 3.45 in the first year and a 2.81 annual average. The 2027 rate is estimated to have no net increase over the prior year. The district does not expect state-program borrowing for debt service. Audited bond proceeds cannot fund salaries, repairs, maintenance or operating expenses.

Authorizes up to $115.985 million in unlimited-tax bonds for school safety, buildings, infrastructure, special education and career additions, technology, sites and buses. Each series may last up to 20 years. Estimated new-bond millage is 1.74 in the first year and a 2.06 annual average. Combined existing and proposed bond debt millage is expected at or below 7.00. The district does not expect state-program borrowing for debt service. Audited bond proceeds cannot fund salaries, repairs, maintenance or operating expenses.

Authorizes up to $47.34 million in unlimited-tax bonds for buildings, facilities, equipment and sites for learning, health, safety, security and energy conservation. Each series may last up to 30 years. Estimated new-bond millage is 2.50 in the first year and a 2.50 annual average. The district does not expect state-program borrowing for debt service. Audited bond proceeds cannot fund salaries, repairs, maintenance or operating expenses.

Replaces 17.26 mills and restores 0.74 mill for a total 18 mills of operating authority for 2026–2035. Principal residences and other legally exempt property are excluded. The prior authorization expires with the 2026 levy; the official question estimates $252,288 in 2026 revenue from the proposal.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the operating millage replacement and restoration.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $165 million in unlimited-tax bonds for buildings and additions, athletic and other facilities, technology, sites, health, safety, security and energy conservation. Each series may last up to 15 years. Estimated new-bond millage is 1.41 in the first year and a 2.05 annual average. Combined existing and proposed bond debt millage is expected at or below 2.20. Audited bond proceeds cannot fund salaries, repairs, maintenance or operating expenses.

Replaces, restores and extends operating-tax authority for 2026–2035, replacing authority scheduled to expire in 2033. Although 22 mills are authorized, no more than 18 may be levied; four mills protect against future constitutional rollbacks. Principal residences and other legally exempt property are excluded. Estimated 2026 revenue is $17,701,778.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the replacement and restoration within the 18 mill levy cap.
